answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small bond that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, rather than trusting a fable about free identities. Like a grove where every tree must put down roots before drawing water, an agent earns reputation only after a history of verified work, and creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because each one needs its own stake and track record. An attacker crossing an open meadow of cheap accounts then faces real cost per identity, so flooding the network stops paying off.
